introduction: In everyday language, 'work' means any physical or mental labor. But in Physics, Work has a very strict definition: Work is only done when a Force applied to an object successfully causes it to move (Displacement) in the direction of the force.

core_concepts.title: Work (W)
core_concepts.description:
Work is the scalar product of Force ($F$) and Displacement ($s$). 
Formula: $W = F \cdot s \cdot \cos(\theta)$, where $\theta$ is the angle between Force and Displacement. 
SI Unit: Joule (J). It is a Scalar quantity.

core_concepts.title: Positive, Negative, and Zero Work
core_concepts.description:
1. Positive Work: Force and displacement are in the SAME direction ($\theta = 0^\circ$). Example: A horse pulling a cart. 
2. Negative Work: Force and displacement are in OPPOSITE directions ($\theta = 180^\circ$). Example: Work done by Friction. 
3. Zero Work: Force and displacement are PERPENDICULAR ($\theta = 90^\circ$). Example: A coolie carrying a load on his head and walking on a horizontal platform. (Gravity pulls down, coolie walks forward; angle is 90°).

core_concepts.title: Energy (E)
core_concepts.description:
Energy is simply the 'capacity to do work'. Whatever work is done on an object is stored in it as Energy. 
SI Unit: Joule (J) - exactly the same as Work. It is a Scalar quantity.

core_concepts.title: Power (P)
core_concepts.description:
Power is the 'Rate of doing work' or the rate at which energy is consumed. 
Formula: $P = \frac{\text{Work}}{\text{Time}} = \frac{W}{t}$. 
SI Unit: Watt (W) or Joules/second.

important_entities.name: Circular Motion and Zero Work
important_entities.significance: When an object moves in a circle (like the Moon around the Earth), the centripetal force is always directed towards the center, while displacement is tangential (90° angle). Hence, the work done by Earth's gravity on the Moon is ZERO.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: 'A man holds a 50 kg weight over his head for 2 hours. How much work has he done?' Answer: ZERO. Because there is NO displacement ($s = 0$), despite the man getting tired.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: 1 Horsepower (HP) = 746 Watts. This is a favorite factual question in Railway and SSC exams.

exam_strategy_tips: Always check the angle in work questions. If a person pushes a wall and the wall doesn't move, Work = 0. If a person walks with a load on his head, Work against gravity = 0.
